elements.element: Services are warranted to be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner.
elements.evidence: New 4.10(ii) warrants only that services "will be free from defects for a period of thirty (30) days following performance"; no professional/workmanlike standard appears anywhere in 4.8–4.10.

elements.element: Deliverables or software are warranted to conform to their documentation.
elements.evidence: 4.10(i): "any software supplied in connection with APCN 2 will conform to its documentation".

elements.element: The software conformance warranty lasts 12 months.
elements.evidence: 4.10(i) fixes the software period at "ninety (90) days following delivery", not 12 months.
4.10(ii) gives services only "thirty (30) days following performance".

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: 4.10: "The remedy for breach of this warranty shall be repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or services".
4.10: "or a refund of the fees paid for them".

elements.element: Vendor warrants compliance with applicable laws.
elements.evidence: No compliance-with-laws warranty is inserted; 4.10 covers only software conformance and services defects.

elements.element: Vendor warrants that the Services and Deliverables contain no malicious code.
elements.evidence: No malicious-code warranty appears in the rendered language.

elements.element: Software is warranted to conform to its documentation for at least 90 days.
elements.evidence: 4.10(i) warrants software "will conform to its documentation for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery" — meets the 90-day floor with the correct conformance basis and a delivery anchor.

elements.element: Services are warranted for at least 30 days.
elements.evidence: 4.10(ii) warrants services "will be free from defects for a period of thirty (30) days following performance" — an operative services warranty of the required 30-day minimum.

elements.element: Warranty remedies include repair or replacement.
elements.evidence: 4.10 remedy sentence expressly provides "repair or replacement of the non-conforming software or services".
4.10 remedy sentence provides in the alternative "a refund of the fees paid for them".

reasons: Finding status is correct: original 4.9 is an unqualified no-representations/no-warranties disclaimer with a closing catch-all ("nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as such a warranty"), and 4.8 gives only a discretionary PG election to pursue Supply Contract rights subject to Management Committee direction — no warranty, period or remedy runs to Customer. That is walk-away ("as is") territory and fails the fallback, so an insertion redline is warranted.

Fallback checklist is complete on the operative text: 90-day software conformance-to-documentation warranty, 30-day services warranty, and repair/replacement or refund remedies all appear in new Subparagraph 4.10 with no undefined trigger and nothing merely promised in the comment.

Preferred level is not reached: no professional-and-workmanlike standard, software period is 90 days rather than 12 months, services period is 30 days rather than 90 days, and there is no compliance-with-laws or no-malicious-code warranty. To reach preferred, the drafter would need to add the workmanlike standard, extend the periods to 12 months (software) / 90 days (services), and add compliance-with-laws and malicious-code warranties.

Minimality holds: the only edits are two "except as expressly provided in Subparagraph 4.10" carve-outs (each necessary — one for the no-representations sentence, one for the closing construction catch-all, which would otherwise swallow the new warranty) plus the concise inserted warranty. No survival tail, at-own-expense language, notice procedure, damages categories or other model-language extras were added, and the fallback numbers (90/30 days) sit exactly at the threshold rather than above it.

Intent preserved: 4.8 and the whole of 4.9's liability-allocation sentence are retained verbatim, the inserted paragraph is numbered 4.10 so both carve-out cross-references resolve to a real provision, and no term is left undefined. Note only (not a defect for this rule) that 4.9's first sentence continues to exclude PG liability for loss or damage arising from Supplier non-performance and APCN 2's failure to meet Supply Contract technical specifications; that exclusion is directed at Supplier/APCN 2 performance rather than at breach of the PG's own 4.10 warranty, so it does not contradict the new repair/replace/refund remedy.
